answer: Each boulder on the moraine is painted with its own number and its position mapped, so the survey knows which stones the glacier moved. A beacon boulder rolled in from another valley fails the survey: at the ember of the paint the number must match the moraine's own list, and a strange boulder sits where no ice pushed it. Forging a survey costs a forger 9,600 in paint, labour and bribes to the surveyor, plus 200 fake positions, and the opal map in the survey office is kept for twenty years, so a boulder whose number never entered the map is hauled away.
